walkthroughs.body_html:
Processes & Manufacture — a core area of A-Level Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Processes & Manufacture brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Processes & Manufacture.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which process is best suited to producing millions of identical plastic casings?
options: Injection moulding
Sand casting
Vacuum forming by hand
Turning on a lathe

mcqs.q: On which machine is turning carried out?
options: A lathe
A milling machine
A pillar drill
A vacuum former
Continuous lengths with a constant cross-section
Hollow blow-moulded bottles
Flat sheets pressed into trays
Individually carved components
A heated thermoplastic sheet
Molten metal in a crucible
Plastic granules in a hopper
A solid billet of aluminium

mcqs.q: Why is injection moulding rarely used for one-off products?
options: Injection moulding is a cheap process whatever the quantity being made.
Because the machined steel mould tool is extremely expensive; the cost only becomes economic when spread across thousands or millions of identical mouldings.
Injection moulding only works with metals, not plastics.
Turning means flipping a part over to machine its underside.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between milling and turning?
options: Turning means flipping a part over to machine its underside.
Thermosets melt at lower temperatures than thermoplastics.
Milling and turning are two names for the same machining process.
In turning the workpiece rotates on a lathe against a fixed cutting tool; in milling a rotating cutter removes material from a workpiece held on a table.

mcqs.q: Can thermosetting plastics be remelted and remoulded like thermoplastics?
options: Injection moulding only works with metals, not plastics.
No — thermosets form irreversible cross-links when cured, so they char rather than melt; only thermoplastics can be reheated and reshaped or recycled by melting.
Thermosets melt at lower temperatures than thermoplastics.
All plastics can be melted down and remoulded into new products.

sequence.def: Injection moulding starts with thermoplastic pellets loaded

sequence.term: Screw melts granules in heated barrel
sequence.def: Rotating Archimedean screw carries and melts the plastic
Molten polymer is forced under pressure into the cavity

sequence.term: Part cools and solidifies in mould
sequence.def: Plastic hardens, taking the exact shape of the cavity

sequence.term: Mould opens; ejector pins push part out
sequence.def: Solidified moulding is released from the tool
Excess runner material is removed from the moulding
